title: Prompt curriculum — progressive templates and failure cases (scratch)
content:
Overview:
This is a personal working doc for designing a "progressive prompt curriculum" — a small library of templates and few-shot example sets that teach the model how to handle a task in stages. Goal is to produce stable, incremental improvements across model versions and to expose brittle failure modes early.

Why curriculum?
- Some downstream tasks (explainers, multi-step reasoning, label normalization) fail unpredictably with single-shot prompts. A staged prompt that starts explicit and gradually abstracts tends to reduce catastrophic regressions.
- Useful for onboarding new models: run stage 1 (verbose scaffolding) as smoke test, stage 3 (compressed template) for cost-sensitive workloads.

Quick plan / experiments to run (RD tickets to create):
- RD-XXXX: baseline: single-shot templated instruction (v0).
- RD-XXXX: curriculum v1: 3-stage prompts (verbose -> targeted -> minimal). Track exact pass/fail on unit eval set.
- RD-XXXX: adversarial probe: swap synonyms, reorder examples, inject distractor context.
- RD-XXXX: few-shot pruning: try 3 vs 5 vs 8 shots, measure latencies + token cost.

Curriculum templates (drafts):
1) Stage A: Scaffolding / Explain-then-do
- Prompt skeleton:
  "You are an assistant that must follow the following steps: 1) Restate the goal in one sentence; 2) List assumptions; 3) Provide the answer with numbered steps; 4) Provide a short summary."
- Use when onboarding new model variants or when the task is underspecified.

2) Stage B: Guided examples (targeted few-shot)
- Prompt skeleton:
  "Below are 3 examples. For each, the user asks X and the assistant responds Y. After the examples answer the new query in the same style."
- Example set should include: 1 canonical positive, 1 near-failure (edge case), 1 adversarial (distractor).

3) Stage C: Minimal instruction (cost-optimized)
- Prompt skeleton:
  "Answer concisely. If ambiguous, ask 1 clarifying question. Format: bullet points with max 6 bullets."
- Use when model has passed Stage A+B tests.

Constructing few-shot sets (principles):
- Diversity: include at least one colloquial phrasing and one technical phrasing.
- Negative examples: include a bad answer for the model to avoid (show-through contrast).
- Edge cases prioritized: 30% of set should be edge/adversarial cases for the domain.
- Label normalization: show canonical label mapping explicitly in 2 examples.

Example few-shot (short) for "extract key actions from an email":
- EX1 (canonical): "Please set up meeting Wednesday 2pm -> Action: schedule meeting, propose time 2025-10-15 14:00"
- EX2 (edge): "Can you loop in legal if needed?" -> "Action: flag legal review, create ticket"
- EX3 (adversarial): email with signatures and unrelated boilerplate -> "Action: identify task lines only"

Failure case catalog (observed / expected tests):
- Hallucinated dates: model invents date when none exists. Test: remove explicit dates; expect 'no date provided'.
- Role-dropping: model ignores role requested (e.g., "act as a tax advisor"). Test: include role in instruction header; expect role-reflective phrasing.
- Overconfident normalization: maps ‘Q2’ to wrong quarter. Test: ambiguous label mapping; expect clarification.
- Token truncation fallout: long examples cause missing final step. Test with long context, compare stage A vs C.

Evaluation heuristics / metrics to capture:
- Task correctness (binary for unit tests).
- Calibration score (confidence vs correctness when model outputs confidence).
- Verbosity metric (tokens generated) to monitor cost.
- Failure mode tags (string list) so we can filter examples (e.g., hallucination, truncation, style mismatch).

Quick checklist for adding a new template to the library:
- [ ] Create minimal spec + examples (3 samples)
- [ ] Add corresponding unit tests (gold answers + expected tags)
- [ ] Run against 3 model families (base, quantized, tuned).
- [ ] Capture token cost and latency.
- [ ] If regression observed, pin to stage A for that customer flow.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider "reverse curriculum": start from minimal and expand only if model fails specific unit tests. Might save tokens on many queries.
- Autosuggest UI: an agent that recommends which stage to route a request to based on short probe (1 token budget probe?). TODO: sketch routing policy.
- Try mixing contrastive examples: show a wrong answer and a corrected answer, see if model avoids the wrong pattern.

Links / references (internal):
- Slack: #prompt-crafting (search: "curriculum")
- Confluence seed: Prompt Library Index (linked above)
- GH: prompts repo tests folder -> /tests/curriculum

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Finalize 3 canonical tasks for pilot (email action extraction, short summarization, slot-filling normalization).
- Build small eval harness (py script) to run stage A/B/C across 4 models and produce a CSV that includes pass/fail + token counts.
- Sync with Ben (examples curation) and María (eval harness infra).

Scratch area (random fragments):
- "If ambiguous, prefer explicit question" vs "If ambiguous, default to most common sense" — need to pick consistent policy per flow.
- Short meta-prompt to put at top: "Follow the style of the examples strictly; do not invent facts."
- Example micro-template for translations + tone preservation.

End of doc (working).
